Chapter 9: Sustaining a Culture of Fairness
Let’s dive into what it really takes to keep fairness alive in an organization—not as a one-time project, but as a living, breathing culture that grows and evolves over time.
Picture this: fairness isn’t something you just check off a list. It’s something you nurture, day after day, as your team and your organization change and expand.
So, how do you actually sustain this kind of culture? Well, there are a few key strategies that really make a difference.
First up: leadership commitment. The people at the top need to consistently walk the talk—modeling fairness in everything they do, and holding themselves accountable if they fall short. Then, there’s continuous learning. It’s important to keep the conversations going with regular training on things like bias, inclusion, and what it really means to manage equitably. Recognition and rewards matter, too. When you celebrate individuals or teams who truly embody fairness, you make it part of your organization’s identity—something everyone wants to be associated with.
And don’t forget about policy review. It’s not just about putting rules in place once and forgetting about them. You’ve got to revisit your policies and practices regularly to make sure they’re still relevant and actually working.
Here’s an image that might help: think of fairness as a garden. If you don’t tend to it, weeds—like bias or inconsistency—can creep in before you know it. You water the soil with feedback, let sunlight in with transparency, and prune with policy reviews. That’s how you keep the culture healthy and vibrant.
Another great way to keep things on track is to create “fairness champions.” These are folks at all levels who keep an eye out for fairness, speak up when something’s off, and help tackle issues early. When everyone feels responsible, fairness stops being just the job of HR or leadership—it becomes a shared commitment.
And remember, a culture of fairness can’t stay static. As your workforce changes, so do the challenges and opportunities. Staying open to fresh ideas and honest feedback keeps the culture dynamic and responsive.
So, if you want fairness to thrive, treat it like a garden—keep nurturing, adapting, and involving everyone. That’s how you build something that lasts.
